tools.name: check_domains
tools.description: Checks whether domain names are available, with registration and renewal prices. Answers come from the registry itself: DNS delegation first, then RDAP, with a WHOIS fallback for the registries that publish no RDAP service. A registry that is throttled, timed out or unreachable is reported as unconf

tools.name: whois
tools.description: Registry record for one domain: registrar, registration and expiry dates, nameservers, status codes, and whether it appears to be for sale. Resolves the correct registry host for the extension itself, and reads RDAP for .dev, .app and other extensions whose operators publish no port-43 whois service

tools.name: list_tlds
tools.description: Every extension this server can check, with registration and renewal price, minimum registration term, and any eligibility restriction on who may register it. Use before check_domains when the extensions to check are not already decided: the catalogue is wider than the handful most people can name,

tools.name: watch_domain
tools.description: Register a watch on a domain that is currently taken, and be emailed once — and only once — when the registry confirms it has become registrable. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "watch_domain" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_domains, list_tlds · Private data: whois · Public sink: check_domains, whois, watch_domain · Destructive: check_domains.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_domains, list_tlds · Private data: whois · Public sink: check_domains, whois, watch_domain · Destructive: check_domains

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
